MGM National Harbor Names Chris Gumiela as New President and COO

Published November 10, 2026 · 3 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

MGM National Harbor has named Chris Gumiela as its new president and chief operating officer, the Maryland property confirmed this week. Gumiela joined MGM Resorts in 2006 through the company's Management Associate Program and has spent more than 20 years across land-based and online operations roles within the company since.

A high-performing property

MGM National Harbor, located just outside Washington, D.C., generated more than $823.2 million in revenue in 2025, making it the second most profitable commercial casino outside the Las Vegas Strip. The resort has 308 hotel rooms and has been one of MGM's steadier regional performers since it opened in Prince George's County, Maryland, in 2016.

The timing: a Sphere project on the way

The appointment comes as MGM National Harbor moves ahead with Sphere National Harbor, a planned $1.4 billion, 6,000-seat venue on 14 acres adjacent to the existing property, developed in partnership with Sphere Entertainment. The project has been described as a scaled-back, regionally sized take on the Las Vegas Sphere concept, and gives the incoming president and COO a major capital project to oversee alongside day-to-day operations at one of MGM's most valuable regional assets.

What it means for the property

Leadership changes at a single regional property don't move betting lines or odds, but they're worth tracking for anyone following the broader health of MGM Resorts' regional casino portfolio, especially with a billion-dollar expansion project now entering a more active phase at this specific site. Our casino guides cover the games and mechanics at properties like this one, independent of who's running the business side.
